answer: The voyage test I would run is Bitcoin OP_RETURN timestamp: a timestamp burned into a Bitcoin transaction, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so a timestamp burned into a Bitcoin transaction stays private; the mirror is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the forge of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
